frames.name: Lucy walks upright
frames.summary: The Australopithecus afarensis skeleton from Hadar in Ethiopia. Bipedal, small-brained, and 600,000 years before anyone knapped a stone.

frames.name: Oldest footprints
frames.summary: Hominins walked across wet volcanic ash at Laetoli in Tanzania and the prints set. The oldest direct record of upright walking, older than any stone tool.

frames.name: First stone tools
frames.summary: The oldest known deliberately knapped stone, at Lomekwi 3 in Kenya. Half a million years before the oldest fossil of our own genus.

frames.name: First Homo fossil
frames.summary: The oldest fossil attributed to our genus, from Ledi-Geraru in Ethiopia.

frames.name: Controlled fire
frames.summary: The earliest secure evidence of fire kept and used on purpose, at Wonderwerk Cave in South Africa.

frames.name: First Homo sapiens
frames.summary: The earliest fossils of our own species, from Jebel Irhoud in Morocco. Roughly a tenth of the way back to the first stone tools.

frames.name: Neanderthals disappear
frames.summary: The last traces of Neanderthals, after some 360,000 years across Europe and western Asia.

frames.name: Last Glacial Maximum
frames.summary: The coldest point of the last Ice Age, when ice sheets reached their greatest extent and sea level was about 120 m lower than today.

frames.name: Start of the Holocene
frames.summary: The end of the last Ice Age and the start of the present geological epoch, 11,700 years before 1950. Farming begins within two thousand years of it, nearly everywhere independently.

frames.name: Life of Jesus
frames.summary: Traditional dates for the life of Jesus of Nazareth.

frames.name: Fall of Western Rome
frames.summary: Deposition of Romulus Augustulus; conventional end of the Western Roman Empire.

frames.name: Fall of Constantinople
frames.summary: Ottoman conquest ends the Byzantine Empire; conventional end of the Middle Ages.

frames.name: Columbus reaches the Americas
frames.summary: Christopher Columbus's first landfall in the Bahamas; the beginning of sustained European contact with the Americas.

frames.name: American Revolution
frames.summary: Colonial revolt that produced the first successful independence movement in the Americas.

frames.name: French Revolution
frames.summary: Overthrew the French monarchy and ancien régime; template for modern political revolutions.

frames.name: World War I
frames.summary: First industrialized total war; collapsed four empires (Russian, German, Austro-Hungarian, Ottoman).

frames.name: World War II
frames.summary: Global war fought in Europe, Asia, and the Pacific; ended with Axis defeat and the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

frames.name: Life of Confucius
frames.summary: Life of the Chinese philosopher Kongzi.

frames.name: Life of the Buddha
frames.summary: Traditional dates (varies by tradition).

frames.name: Qin Unification of China
frames.summary: Qin Shi Huangdi ended the Warring States period and founded the first unified Chinese empire.

frames.name: Meiji Restoration
frames.summary: Ended the Tokugawa shogunate and restored imperial authority under Emperor Meiji; launched Japan's rapid modernization.

frames.name: Founding of the PRC
frames.summary: Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic of China after Communist victory in the Chinese Civil War.

frames.name: Life of Muhammad
frames.summary: Life of the Prophet Muhammad, founder of Islam. His flight from Mecca to Medina in 622 marks Year 1 of the Islamic calendar.

frames.name: The Hijra (Muhammad's migration)
frames.summary: Year 1 of the Islamic calendar.

frames.name: Mongol Sack of Baghdad
frames.summary: Hülegü Khan's Mongols destroyed Baghdad and ended the Abbasid Caliphate; a symbolic close to the Islamic Golden Age.

frames.name: Ashoka's conversion (Kalinga War)
frames.summary: Mauryan emperor Ashoka's remorse after the bloody conquest of Kalinga led him to embrace Buddhism and pacifism.

frames.name: Indian Independence & Partition
frames.summary: End of the British Raj; partition into independent India and Pakistan produced one of history's largest forced migrations.

frames.name: Great Pyramid of Giza built
frames.summary: Traditional date of the Great Pyramid of Khufu at Giza; the oldest of the Seven Wonders and the only one still standing.

frames.name: Mansa Musa's Hajj
frames.summary: Mansa Musa of Mali's pilgrimage to Mecca was so lavish it crashed Egyptian gold prices for a decade.

frames.name: Battle of Adwa
frames.summary: Ethiopian victory over Italy; kept Ethiopia the only major African state to remain uncolonized in the age of European empires.

frames.name: Cahokia at peak
frames.summary: Mississippian city near modern St. Louis; the largest pre-Columbian settlement in North America.

frames.name: Fall of Tenochtitlan
frames.summary: Spanish conquistadors under Cortés, allied with Tlaxcala and other indigenous nations, took the Aztec capital.

frames.name: Fall of the Inca
frames.summary: Pizarro executed Atahualpa; effective end of the Inca Empire, though the Vilcabamba state resisted until 1572.

frames.name: Settlement of Aotearoa (Māori)
frames.summary: Approximate date of first Polynesian settlement of New Zealand; last major landmass on Earth to be settled by humans.

frames.name: Cook's first Pacific voyage
frames.summary: James Cook's HMS Endeavour voyage mapped New Zealand and the eastern coast of Australia.

frames.name: Origin of agriculture
frames.summary: Independent agricultural revolutions began around this time in the Fertile Crescent, China, and Mesoamerica.

frames.name: Origin of writing
frames.summary: Earliest known writing systems: Sumerian cuneiform and Egyptian hieroglyphs.

frames.name: Battle of Waterloo
frames.summary: Napoleon's final defeat; the reset point for 19th-century European order.

frames.name: Fall of Granada
frames.summary: End of Muslim rule in Iberia; completion of the Reconquista.

frames.name: Siege of Vienna
frames.summary: High-water mark of Ottoman expansion into Europe under Suleiman the Magnificent.

frames.name: Founding of the Mughal Empire
frames.summary: Babur's victory at Panipat established Mughal rule in northern India.

frames.name: First Opium War
frames.summary: British defeat of Qing China; opened the treaty-port century and marked China's decline.

frames.name: Atomic bombing of Hiroshima
frames.summary: First combat use of a nuclear weapon; helped end WWII in the Pacific.

frames.name: Apollo 11 Moon Landing
frames.summary: First human landing on the Moon.

frames.name: Fall of the Berlin Wall
frames.summary: Symbolic end of the Cold War division of Europe.

frames.name: September 11 Attacks
frames.summary: al-Qaeda attacks on the United States; catalyst for the War on Terror.
